questions.q: Why is transport a key sector of the tourism industry?
o: All tourists need some form of transport; tourism cannot exist without it
Transport is the cheapest part of a trip
questions.d: Transportation is a key sector because all tourists require some form of transport.
questions.w: Travel is part of every tourism trip.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three modes of transportation in tourism?
questions.d: Modes of transportation in tourism: water, land and air.
questions.w: Pipelines carry goods like oil, not tourists.

questions.q: Ferry services and inland water transport are examples of:
questions.d: Water transport: short sea routes (ferries, inland transport) and long-haul routes (cruise ships).
questions.w: Ferries cover short distances.

questions.q: A cruise ship provides:
questions.d: Cruise ship: provides transportation and accommodation services.
questions.w: Passengers travel and sleep on the same ship.

questions.q: How many cruise tourists visited Oman in 2019?
questions.d: Cruises in Oman: 383,488 cruise tourists in 2019, a 49.5% increase on 2018.
questions.w: 1.5 million is the number of vehicles; 15,230 km is the road network.

questions.q: Which is one of Oman's famous cruise ports listed on the slides?
questions.d: Famous cruise ports in Oman: Sultan Qaboos Port, Khasab Port and Salalah Port.
questions.w: The other options are airports.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of water transport?
o: It uses relatively little power and can carry large numbers of vehicles
It is faster than air travel
questions.d: Water transport advantages: little power, much larger vessels, high comfort (cruise ships), large vehicle capacity.
questions.w: Water transport is slow compared with air.

questions.q: Which is the most common form of tourism transport for domestic travel and short international trips?
questions.d: Land transport: by far the most common form for domestic travel and short international trips.
questions.w: Cars and buses dominate short trips.

questions.q: Package tours, day tours, airport transfers and inter-city travel commonly use:
questions.d: Bus: used for package tours, day tours, airport transfers and inter-city travel.
questions.w: These are the listed bus uses.

questions.q: Which land transport, like a cruise ship, combines transportation and accommodation?
questions.d: Caravan: campervans combine transportation and accommodation.
questions.w: You can drive and sleep in a campervan.

questions.q: Which is an ADVANTAGE of land transport by car?
o: It is always the fastest mode
questions.d: Land transport advantages: comfort, privacy, flexibility in timing, choice of itineraries, door-to-door service. Disadvantage: congestion.
questions.w: Congestion is its listed disadvantage.

questions.q: According to the slides, Oman's road network in 2018 extended to about:
questions.d: Land transport in Oman: more than 1.5 million vehicles (2020); road network of 15,230 km (2018).
questions.w: 383,488 is the number of cruise tourists.

questions.q: Since 1950, which mode has had the most impact on international tourism?
questions.d: Air transport has had the most impact on international tourism and the structure of the travel industry since 1950.
questions.w: Few places are now more than 24 hours' flying time apart.

questions.q: Which is NOT a reason the airline industry is heavily regulated?
o: To make every flight free for tourists
questions.d: Reasons for regulation: passenger safety, social and environmental concerns, protection of national economic interests.
questions.w: The primary aim of aviation policy is to enhance and protect national interests.

questions.q: Which is one of the regulatory forms used to control the airline industry?
questions.d: Regulatory forms: licensing of airlines, regulation of international operations, regulation of domestic operations.
questions.w: Star grading relates to accommodation.

questions.q: Which is an ADVANTAGE of air transport?
o: A direct line of flight not blocked by mountains, oceans or deserts
It needs only a small terminal
questions.d: Air advantages: direct flight path unimpeded by natural barriers, superior speed, high passenger capacity.
questions.w: The other options are the opposite of its disadvantages.

questions.q: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of air transport?
o: It is vulnerable to terrorism and fluctuating oil prices
questions.d: Air disadvantages: needs a large terminal area, relatively expensive, negative environmental impacts, vulnerable to terrorism and oil prices.
questions.w: Speed and capacity are advantages of air transport.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Oman's five operational civil airports?
questions.d: Oman's airports: Muscat International, Salalah, Duqm, Sohar and Ras Al-Hadd.
questions.w: Nizwa is not on the list.

questions.q: Oman Airports is:
o: A government-owned company that manages and operates Oman's civil airports
questions.d: Oman Airports: government-owned; integrated airport operations and infrastructure (terminals, cargo, runways, parking).
questions.w: It runs airports, not flights.

questions.q: In Faulks' elements of a transport system, roads, railways, airspace and water are:
questions.d: Faulks (1990): the way, the terminal, the carrying unit and motive power.
questions.w: The way is the path the vehicle travels on.

questions.q: Hubs and gateways are examples of which element of a transport system?
questions.d: Terminal: terminals, hubs and gateways where journeys start, end or connect.
questions.w: Hubs are terminals.

questions.q: Aircraft, boats, cars and buses are which element of a transport system?
questions.d: Carrying unit: the vehicle that carries passengers.
questions.w: The vehicle itself is the carrying unit.

questions.q: Oil, hydrogen, bio-fuels and electricity are which element of a transport system?
questions.d: Motive power: the energy that moves the carrying unit.
questions.w: Fuel and energy provide the power.

questions.q: By the late 1960s, most of the long-haul market on the North Atlantic routes had been lost by water transport to:
questions.d: Water transport is slow compared with air travel.
questions.w: Faster air travel took over long-haul routes.

questions.q: Water transport is fast compared with air travel.
questions.d: Water transport is slow compared with air travel.
questions.w: That is why airlines took over long-haul routes.

questions.q: Few parts of the world are now more than 24 hours' flying time from any other part.
questions.d: Air transport has made almost every part of the world reachable within 24 hours.
questions.w: This is why air transport changed international tourism.

questions.q: The airline industry is lightly regulated and simple to operate.
questions.d: The airline industry is heavily regulated and controlled, which makes it complex.
questions.w: Safety, environmental and national interests all require regulation.

questions.q: Land transport can lead to congestion.
questions.d: Congestion is the listed disadvantage of land transport.
questions.w: Many private vehicles crowd the roads.

questions.q: Cruise tourists to Oman in 2019 increased by 49.5% compared with 2018.
questions.d: Cruises in Oman: 383,488 cruise tourists in 2019, a 49.5% increase.
questions.w: This shows the growth of cruise tourism in Oman.

questions.q: Air transport has significant negative environmental impacts.
questions.d: Air disadvantages include significant negative environmental impacts and high energy needs.
questions.w: Social and environmental concerns are also a reason for regulation.

questions.q: Explain the three modes of transportation in tourism and their forms.
questions.a:
1. Water transport: short sea routes (ferries, inland transport) and long-haul routes (cruise ships, which also provide accommodation).
2. Land transport: the most common for domestic and short international trips; cars (private, rented, taxis, limousines), buses (package tours, day tours, transfers, inter-city), rail (some journeys are attractions) and caravans (transport plus accommodation).
3. Air transport: the mode with the most impact on international tourism since 1950; heavily regulated.
questions.d: Modes of transportation: water, land and air.
questions.w: Give the forms of each mode and one key fact about it.

questions.q: Identify the advantages and disadvantages of air transport.
questions.a:
Advantages:
- Direct line of flight not blocked by natural barriers (mountains, oceans, deserts, jungles).
- Superior speed.
- High passenger capacity.
Disadvantages:
- Needs a large terminal area.
- Relatively expensive (high energy needs and safety standards).
- Significant negative environmental impacts.
- Vulnerable to terrorism and fluctuating oil prices.
questions.d: Air transport: the mode with the greatest impact on international tourism.
questions.w: Present them as two lists from the slides' table.

questions.q: Explain why the airline industry is heavily regulated and the forms this regulation takes.
questions.a:
Reasons:
1. Passenger safety.
2. Social and environmental concerns about airline operations.
3. Protection of national economic interests; the primary objective of aviation policy is to enhance and protect national interests.
Regulatory forms:
1. Licensing of airlines.
2. Regulation of international airline operations.
3. Regulation of domestic airline operations.
questions.d: Regulation: rules and controls governments place on the airline industry.
questions.w: Explain the reasons first, then the forms.

questions.q: Explain Faulks' (1990) elements of a transport system, with examples.
questions.a:
1. The way: the path travelled, e.g. roads, railways, tramways, cableways, airspace and water.
2. The terminal: where journeys start, end or connect, e.g. terminals, hubs and gateways.
3. The carrying unit: the vehicle, e.g. aircraft, boats, cars and buses.
4. Motive power: the energy, e.g. coal, oil, hydrogen, bio-fuels and electricity.
questions.d: Transport system: the key elements every transport mode needs.
questions.w: Every journey needs all four: a path, a terminal, a vehicle and power.

questions.q: Describe water transport, including its routes, cruise tourism in Oman and its advantages.
questions.a:
Water transport is slow compared with air; by the late 1960s airlines had taken most North Atlantic long-haul traffic.
Routes: short sea routes (ferries, inland transport) and long-haul routes (cruise ships).
Cruises in Oman: 383,488 cruise tourists in 2019 (49.5% more than 2018); main ports are Sultan Qaboos Port, Khasab Port and Salalah Port.
Advantages: uses relatively little power; can be built much larger than vehicles or aircraft; high comfort on cruise ships; carries large numbers of motor vehicles.
questions.d: Water transport: travel by sea and inland waterways.
questions.w: Include the Oman facts from the slides.

questions.q: Describe land transport, its advantages and disadvantages, and land transport in Oman.
questions.a:
Land transport is the most common form for domestic travel and short international trips.
Forms: cars (private, rented, taxis, limousines), buses, rail and caravans.
Advantages: comfort, privacy, flexibility in timing, choice of itineraries, door-to-door service.
Disadvantage: congestion.
Oman: more than 1.5 million vehicles in 2020; road network of 15,230 km in 2018.
questions.d: Land transport: travel by road and rail.
questions.w: Link the advantages to why land transport is so common.
